evidence.s1_requirements: Every point in steps/1.md is met. `snapshot()` returns `{version, definition, root}` built only from plain values (src/BehaviourTree.ts snapshot(); src/nodes/*/getSnapshot). `TreeSnapshot` is exported as a type (src/index.ts export type block). `restore()` validates, then sets node state (BehaviourTree.ts restore). A snapshot keeps: node state (Node.getSnapshot), children (Composite/Decorator.getSnapshot), repeat and retry counts and targets (Repeat.ts and Retry.ts getSnapshot: iterationCount/targetIterationCount, attemptCount/targetAttemptCount), the lotto pick (Lotto.ts selectedChild index), and the wait's totalDuration/waitedDuration (Wait.ts:112-127). Remaining-time semantics hold for both modes: Wait.ts:150-161 sets `initialUpdateTime = now - waitedDuration`, and in delta mode waitedDuration is the value from the last update. Finished trees restore as finished, and `step()` resets them as usual. The README has an API section and a full example (README 'Saving and Restoring a Tree').
evidence.s1_correctness: Each node type handles its own state correctly. The lotto pick is kept as an index and re-picked only when READY (Lotto.ts:43). Repeat and retry targets are restored, so the random count is not drawn again. A clock-mode wait counts the time since the last step at snapshot time and none of the time before restore (Wait.ts:122-125, 160). A delta-mode wait never reads getDeltaTime during restore, and the test asserts this (SnapshotTestUtilities.ts:196). A settled promise is kept with the same error text, because `String(value)` matches the `${value}` in Action.ts:89. A stale promise is ignored through updatePromiseId, which restore increments (Action.ts restoreSnapshot). Guards and callbacks need no state, and an indefinite wait (totalDuration null) is handled. The test harness snapshots after every step of 17 scenarios, restores a week later, and compares node states and the order of agent calls, for composites, flip/succeed/fail, repeat/retry (fixed and random), lotto, waits (clock, random, delta, indefinite), parallel/race, guards and callbacks, and JSON definitions. In step 1, restore called onNodeStateChange; this was only removed in step 3.
evidence.s2_validation: The definition fingerprint (src/BehaviourTreeDefinitionFingerprint.ts) canonicalises the definition the way the builder reads it: branches are inlined as in BehaviourTreeBuilder.ts:208-209, args default to [], succeedOnAbort to false, lotto weights default to 1 (the same `|| 1` as Lotto.ts:49), and keys are sorted. It is hashed with cyrb53 when the tree is built, so registered subtrees are included. restore throws "snapshot does not match the tree's definition, ..." (BehaviourTree.ts restore). It rejects null, primitives, arrays and objects missing the fields (isObject, version and definition checks) before anything changes, and it validates the whole tree before writing to it. Tests cover 11 different definitions, a different registered subtree, MDSL vs JSON in both directions, whitespace and comments, root order, unused roots, and 11 non-snapshot inputs, each checking the tree is unchanged. A pending promise is saved as READY (Action.ts getSnapshot), with 12 wrapper-node tests plus entry-callback and stale-promise tests. The limitation is documented in README 'Snapshots and promise-based actions' and under Promise-based Actions. One weak spot: the `changes` array in the non-snapshot tests (spec:997, 1006) is never wired to onNodeStateChange, so that assertion checks nothing.
evidence.s3_fixes: Report 1 is fixed at its cause. The notifications array and the onStateChanged calls are removed from every restoreSnapshot override, and Node.restoreSnapshot now assigns `_state` directly (step3.patch Node.ts:545-555, BehaviourTree.ts:526-531). The agent's own step-2 tests that asserted the old behaviour were replaced with tests that restore makes no calls and that the next step reports changes as usual (spec:659-737). The harness also asserts `restored.log` is empty (SnapshotTestUtilities.ts:197). For report 2, the step-1 code already copied every value (Action.ts `{ ...promiseResult }`, fresh objects in each getSnapshot), and the harness already checked snapshot-after-restore equality. So the agent added only regression tests, over all scenarios and settled promises (spec:1128-1195), in a separate test commit. No unrelated source changes.
evidence.design: Each node class overrides getSnapshot, validateSnapshot and restoreSnapshot for its own fields, and the base classes handle state and children (Node.ts, Composite.ts, Decorator.ts). Validation runs before any change, which is what makes the 'tree unchanged' guarantee hold. The fingerprint reuses createRootNodeDefinitionMap and MAIN_ROOT_NODE_KEY rather than duplicating them, but this required exporting builder internals (BehaviourTreeBuilder.ts:57,62,270). The public surface is wider than needed: eight snapshot types are exported from index.ts, not just TreeSnapshot. Many `as NodeSnapshot` / `as { [key: string]: unknown }` casts weaken the typing. The unrequested `_activity` re-entrancy guard rewraps step() and reset() (BehaviourTree.ts:104-136). Naming and JSDoc follow the repository's style.
evidence.tests: A new test/BehaviourTreeSnapshot.spec.ts and a SnapshotTestUtilities.ts use mocha, chai and sinon fake timers, like the existing tests. SnapshotHarness.checkRestoredTreeMatchesOriginal checks a JSON round trip, plain values, node states, the snapshot of the restored tree, no delta-time reads and no calls during restore, and identical later behaviour, for every snapshot point. Edge cases are covered: random choices kept, remaining wait time in both modes and across modes, finished trees re-randomising, settled, rejected and stale promises, and validation errors with exact messages. A baseline Action.spec.ts test was added for the superseded-promise fix. No existing test was removed or weakened; the only tests removed in step 3 were the agent's own tests of the old onNodeStateChange behaviour. Minor: one dead `changes` assertion.
evidence.docs: The README adds a feature bullet, snapshot()/restore() API entries, a full 'Saving and Restoring a Tree' section with a working example (definition, createTree, snapshot, write, read, restore), a sample snapshot JSON, the restore semantics, and the promise limitation next to the API. It is detailed and accurate to the code, if long. The Version History has 4.4.0 (feature plus the action-promise fix) and 4.4.1 (the onNodeStateChange fix), in the table's existing 'Fixed issue where ...' style. package.json and package-lock went to 4.4.0 then 4.4.1. Step 2 correctly has no bump because it came before the release. The step-3 README change replaces the restore bullet that described notifications.
evidence.process: Twelve commits, each with a clear conventional message. Feature, docs, fix and test commits are separate, and dist rebuilds are their own commits (`build: rebuild dist for 4.4.0`). Step 2 is split into the definition check and the pending-promise change, and step 3 into a test commit and a fix commit. No new dependencies; the hash is written inline. Some work went beyond the steps: a baseline Action promise-supersede fix (959f56d, arguably needed for restore's stale-promise handling), the step/reset re-entrancy guard, and a version field in the snapshot. Step 1 also first made snapshot() throw on pending promises and made restore notify, both reversed later.

strengths: Each node type has correct per-node snapshot, validate and restore methods. Restore validates everything before changing anything, so a rejected restore leaves the tree exactly as it was.

A thorough test harness snapshots after every step of 17 scenarios, round-trips through JSON, restores a week later, and asserts identical node states and agent call order, with no calls during restore.

The definition fingerprint canonicalises MDSL and JSON the way the builder reads them, including inlined branches and registered subtrees, and is well tested for equivalence and mismatch. The README and versioning follow the repository's conventions.
issues: The public and internal API is wider than needed: eight snapshot types are exported instead of just TreeSnapshot, builder internals are exported for the fingerprint, and many `as` casts weaken the type safety of the snapshot code.

Some scope creep: the step/reset re-entrancy guard (`_activity`) and a baseline Action promise fix were not asked for, though both are defensible and tested. Step 1 also first shipped behaviour (restore notifying onNodeStateChange, snapshot throwing on pending promises) that later steps reversed.
There are small test gaps: the `changes` array in the non-snapshot rejection tests is never wired to onNodeStateChange, so that assertion checks nothing.
review.verdict: This work meets every requirement across the three steps: per-node snapshots, definition fingerprinting, all-or-nothing validation, the pending-promise limitation, and the onNodeStateChange fix. A strong behavioural-equivalence harness and README docs that follow the repository's conventions back it up. I would merge it after trimming the exported surface and builder exports, and fixing the dead test assertion.
